docs: Curation layer on top of the GitHub API. The page lists every public repository automatically; this file only adds what the API cannot express. Any repo missing here still shows up, using its GitHub description. featured: pinned to the top, in this order. overrides: title (display name), blurb (replaces the GitHub description), demo (live link), tags (extra labels beside the GitHub topics), hidden (true to leave it out). private: repositories that are not public, written here by hand (title, blurb, tags, status). Private repositories are never read automatically: one only appears if it is written here. When it becomes public, the API lists it and this entry stops being used as a private card.

luxury_wheels.title: Luxury Wheels
luxury_wheels.blurb: Final project of my Python course, built and defended: a vehicle-rental platform. A Flask REST API with SQLAlchemy and JWT auth holds every business rule; the vanilla JavaScript front end only consumes it.

deep-learning-specialization.blurb: Coursework for my Deep Learning specialization, on a laptop CPU. The headline: a 422K-parameter CNN I built by hand matches a pre-trained ResNet50 that is 56x larger and takes 16x longer to train.

aftersales-scorecard.title: Aftersales web panel
aftersales-scorecard.blurb: A web app, in development at work, that gathers and controls the aftersales department's information in one place. It automates the service-level evaluation and proposes stock optimizations for the stockholding brands, and runs a machine learning tournament in which models compete to produce the best forecast for each brand. The Power BI reports are already in use.
aftersales-scorecard.status: In development · Power BI reports in use

jarvis-nlu.title: Jarvis NLU
jarvis-nlu.blurb: Final project of my Deep Learning specialization: understanding what a European-Portuguese voice assistant is being asked, across 60 intents. Four networks trained from scratch and compared with paired significance tests. The simplest won, and nothing more complex did significantly better: 83% accuracy at 7 ms per sentence.
